objective: Preserve ZTerm runtime behavior while restructuring the Android client and embedded daemon into AppSDK-governed modules with typed data, control, debug, and plugin boundaries.

boundary.payload_control_separation: confirmed: AppSDK lifecycle, routing, review, promotion, freeze, and SDK lock facts are control resources only; ZTerm request and response payloads cannot carry or reconstruct them.

acceptance_criteria: sdk.lock pins the AppSDK binary and bundle.
AppSDK installs project docs, rules, skills, maps, and contracts.
Active exposes only immutable library artifacts.
Generated artifacts are produced only by AppSDK/compiler.
Protected source is Git-auditable and recoverable.
No project-local sdk.bin becomes an execution entry point.
ZTerm Android client behavior and request/response payload semantics remain unchanged.
Client and daemon module ownership follows android/docs/resource-registry.json, module-registry.json, edge-registry.json, function-map.md, and mainline-call-map.json.
Data, control, debug, and error messages use physically separated typed contracts and registered adjacent edges.
Runtime foundation nodes expose bounded debug subscriptions and versioned snapshots without leaking debug state into business payloads.
The client is composed through a capability-scoped plugin host while terminal frame, buffer, renderer, input, and daemon hot paths remain direct typed nodes.
non_goals: Do not modify business pipeline semantics.
Do not modify request or response payload semantics.
Do not introduce a second compiler.
Do not refactor Mac, Windows, or wterm runtime in this migration.
Do not use Cordis as the terminal frame, buffer apply, mirror capture, transport, or input hot-path event bus.
assumptions: The AppSDK project root remains android/ because it contains both the current Android client and embedded daemon mainline.
packages/shared/** is admitted only for shared typed contracts required by the registered Android/daemon edges.
Existing runtime source remains read-only until the AppSDK goal, maps, gates, and a Playground slice identify a unique owner and promotion unit.
